0.0.n: A neutral, broadly polite way to refer to yourself.

0.2.n: Marks the speaker as another person who has drawn something.

0.3.n: Past form of 描ける, the can-do form of 描く, expressing successful completion here.

1.0.n: An informal call to draw someone's attention to something.

2.0.n: Points to the drawing being shown.

2.2.n: The first part of the character's name ポン太郎, not a separate word here.

2.3.n: The rest of the name ポン太郎; 太郎 is a common element in male names.

2.4.n: A casual form of でしょう, used here to ask for confirmation.

3.0.n: 偉い plus そう describes seeming self-important; な connects this description to 感じ.

3.1.n: Refers to the impression or air the drawing conveys.

3.2.n: Identifies the arrogant-looking impression as what closely resembles the character.

3.3.n: Describes a very close resemblance; the person being compared is understood from context.

4.0.n: A self-reference commonly used by boys and men.

4.1.n: After 僕, の stands in for the omitted drawing, making 僕の mean the speaker's drawing.

4.2.n: Adds the speaker's drawing to the things the listener should look at.

4.3.n: The て-form of 見る acts as a casual request here.

5.0.n: The opening of うわあ, an exclamation of surprise or excitement.

5.1.n: This あ stretches out うわ into うわあ; it is not a separate word here.

5.3.n: Names what the speaker recognizes in the drawing.

6.0.n: かっこいい describes an impressive appearance, and でしょ invites the listener to agree.

7.0.n: This is part of the name とりっぴい, not a form of the verb とる.

7.1.n: Completes the name とりっぴい; も adds too, できてる means is finished, and よ draws attention to the news.

0.tip: 描けた emphasizes successfully getting the drawing done, rather than simply having drawn.

1.tip: ほら calls attention to something without using a verb for looking.

2.tip: でしょ asks the listener to confirm something the speaker already suspects.

3.lit: The arrogant-looking vibe is exactly alike!
3.tip: 偉そう means looking self-important here, not looking admirable.

4.tip: 僕の can stand alone as mine when the possessed object is clear.

5.tip: うわあ is one drawn-out exclamation, even though the word list splits it.

6.tip: でしょ after an adjective seeks agreement about that description.

7.lit: Torippi too, is finished, you know.
7.tip: できてる is casual できている, describing a finished result; context tells us it is Torippi's drawing.
